 The Stanford Cardinal (4-1) will look to continue a four-game home win streak when they host the Sacramento State Hornets (1-2) on November 19, 2026 at Maples Pavilion.
 On Tuesday, in its most recent game, Stanford topped UC Irvine 65-61. With 13 points, Austin Maurer was its leading scorer. In its most recent game, Sacramento State lost to UC Davis on Saturday, 75-56. Its top scorer was Marcus Wilson with 12 points.
 When is Stanford vs. Sacramento State and when does it start?
 This game between the Cardinal and Hornets will take place on Thursday, November 19, 2026. You should expect the opening tip at 10 p.m. ET.
 Where to Watch Stanford vs. Sacramento State
 The Cardinal and Hornets will hit the floor at Maples Pavilion for this matchup on Nov. 19, and if you would like to catch the matchup live, get your tickets now from Vivid Seats ! 
 What channel is the game on?
 You can catch this game live on ACC Network Extra.
 Watch the Stanford vs. Sacramento State live stream on Fubo
 Live Stream Online: Sign up for Fubo today! 
 Stanford Cardinal vs. Sacramento State Hornets Game Preview
 Stanford Stats, Odds & Insights
 Stanford has a +41 scoring differential, topping opponents by 8.2 points per game. It is putting up 75.8 points per game to rank 222nd in college basketball and is allowing 67.6 per contest to rank 98th in college basketball.
 The Cardinal post just 1.5 fewer points than the Hornets give up (77.3).
 Stanford knocks down two more threes per contest than the opposition, 7.2 (243rd in college basketball) compared to its opponents’ 5.2.
 Sacramento State Stats, Odds & Insights (2025-26)
 Sacramento State was ranked 128th in college basketball offensively last season with 77.7 points per game, while defensively it was 10th-worst (82 points allowed per game). 
 The Hornets scored an average of 77.7 points per game last year, only 4.7 more points than the 73 the Cardinal gave up.
 Sacramento State sank 7.5 three-pointers per game (199th-ranked in college basketball) last year, while putting up a 33.3% three-point percentage (215th-ranked).
 At home, the Hornets averaged 86.6 points per game last season. On the road, they scored 71.9.
